newsitem.title: USA: U.S. property insurers helped by mild Q2.
newsitem.headline: U.S. property insurers helped by mild Q2.

text.p: Most U.S. property-casualty insurers are set to report higher second quarter earnings, helped by the relatively mild weather this spring.
Insured catastrophe losses in this year's second quarter were light at only $980 million compared with $1.7 billion last year, according to Property Claim Services.
Tornadoes and hail storms tend to be the biggest catastrophic threat in the second quarter, but activity this year declined markedly in comparison with last year.
"From a weather perspective, this quarter should be fairly good for the industry," Merrill Lynch analyst Jay Cohen said.
The gentle spring followed an almost equally mild winter, when catastrophe losses totalled just $860 million compared with $2.55 billion a year ago.

And more than a month into the Atlantic hurricane season, so far storm activity has been fairly quiet. Catastrophe losses in last year's third quarter totalled $2.23 billion, mainly from Hurricane Fran, which struck North Carolina in September.
Overall, U.S. property-casualty insurers are expected to post operating profit growth of 13 percent in the second quarter, according to First Call.
That compares with a forecast for second quarter operating profit growth of 9.1 percent for the Standard & Poor's 500, First Call said.
But U.S. auto insurers are expected to turn in some of the insurance industry's best second quarter results as the number and cost of claims remains low.
"The claims environment is still fairly favorable" for auto insurers, Cohen said.
Big auto insurers like Allstate Corp, Progressive Corp, and Mercury General Corp "that have an edge with distribution or a low cost structure ... will probably have a good quarter," he said.
But commercial property-casualty insurers will be challenged to show premium growth as a highly competitive environment keeps pricing low, prompting many carriers to decline the business.
"Everybody knows it's a tough environment," Dillon Read analyst Michael Lewis said.
Even so, he said, he expects it to be "a decent quarter considering the competitive pressures that are coming to bear on the industry and slow growth of the industry."
Commercial insurers such as American International Group Inc and Chubb Corp with specialty niches are likely to outperform their rivals, Merrill's Cohen said.
Meanwhile, life insurers are expected to post average operating profit growth of 12 percent, First Call said.
Strong variable annuity and life sales will help to drive that earnings growth, Schroder & Co Inc analyst Andrew Kligerman said.
In addition, earnings will be helped by variable annuity and life market appreciation and by flat to lower interest rates, which have helped to improve margin spreads, he said.
"Looking at the second quarter, I would say the outlook is positive," he said.
